To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the threshold current and the optical scattering losses are significantly increased when the waveguide of ( Al,Ga )As double‐hetrostructure lasers contains growth defects such as terraces and menisci.

the active layer of (Al, Ga) As double heterostructure laser material is not always uniform, that optical scattering losses can be caused by the nonuniformities, and that the losses can be computed from the characterizations of the nonuniformities.

the threshold current of (Al,Gal)As double‐ heterostructure lasers is strongly dependent on variations in the thickness of the active‐layer guide and that the optical‐scattering losses due to these thickness variations are a function of the parameters which characterize the local waveguide deformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and modeling of the effects of active‐layer waveguidedefects in (Al,Gal)As double‐ heterostructure laser diodes.
the effects of growth‐related defects in (Al,Gal)As double‐ heterostructure laser material and their influence on laser performance.
the characterization and modeling of optical scattering in (Al,GalAs double‐hetersostructure laser material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the threshold current variations of (Al,Gal)As double‐ heterostructure lasers are caused by the optical scattering losses which are introduced into the active layer by growth defects.

the optical scattering losses in a laser can be reduced to a negligible level if the epitaxial growth of the active‐layer material is controlled so that the thickness variations are less than about 0.5% of the active‐region thickness.
the optical scattering loss in (Al,Gas)As double‐ heterostructure laser material is a function of the growth defect density and of the severity of the individual defects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the V‐threshold current variations are caused by the optical scattering losses which are induced in the laser by growth defects in the active layer.
the optical scattering loss in (Al,GaNAs) DH lasers is dominated by the scattering from growth‐related defects.
we have shown that the threshold currents of (Al,Gal)As DH lasers can be significantly affected by growth defects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optical scattering losses due to growth‐related waveguide deformations are significant in (Al,Gal)As double‐ heterostructure lasers, and are comparable to or greater than the scattering losses due to surface and facet imperfections.
the V _{th} current of the DH laser is not only determined by the active layer thickness but also the active layer waveguide.
the optical scattering losses in double heterostructure lasers are not necessarily a constant value.
